name: Pair-twined basketry at Kfar Samir
description: Three twig basket fragments from the central sector of submerged Kfar Samir preserve alternate pair-twining. Excavators found them in a clay-filled pit containing olive stones and wood fragments.

places.note: Kfar Samir, central sector, Carmel coast.

date.label: 5000–4730 cal BCE (reported)
date.basis: The 2007 excavation report assigns radiocarbon sample RT 4689 to the braiding. Its figures identify the fragments later labelled KS 2. The report omits the calibration probability, and later accounts give inconsistent or broader dates.

events.statement: Three waterlogged twig fragments catalogued as KS 2 preserve alternate pair-twining. They came from a clay-filled pit with dozens of olive stones.

evidence.locator: Winter 1994 pit, Figs. 3–5 and sample RT 4689
evidence.supports: Documents recovery, identifies the three conserved fragments and gives a calibrated date from the braiding itself.
Describes the weave and findspot, reproduces the 2007 field photograph and assigns an age using the site chronology.

events.caveats: The original RT 4689 assay documentation has not been located. A 2013 account assigns a different interval to the basket, which a 2017 table assigns to a distinct pit-8 mat. The 2023 account gives a site date. See the provenance review for the figure and sample comparisons.

earliest_record.rationale: Reported direct date on the surviving pair-twined braiding, identified through the excavation and later object photographs.

caveats: The excavators proposed that the basket may have held or strained olives during oil extraction. The fragments were recovered in a separate pit from the installation with crushed olive stones and pulp.
